title: Heuristic Composer — personal scratchlog
content:
High-level idea (one-liner): lightweight in-console "heuristic composer" that lets product engineers assemble small, auditable inference policies (cost/latency gates, safety filters, scoring transforms) and apply them per-route or per-customer without code deploys.

Why: ops/PD are constantly tweaking ad-hoc rules in code or lambda layers. We need an authorable policy layer that is simple (no heavy rule engine), composable, and observable. This can reduce incidents where a change to routing or fallback logic requires infra rollout. It also democratizes quick experiments (A/B a cheap gating heuristic vs full model switch).

Core constraints:
- Must be tiny DSL or JSON config (no Java-like rules). Prefer declarative named predicates + actions.
- Runtime must evaluate per-request within 500us extra p99 over baseline on Hosted API for small policies.
- Policies versioned, diffable, and rollouts support: local canary, target subset of customers, fallback policy on eval error.
- Safety first: composition must be monotonic (no accidental bypass).
- Auditing: who changed, why (free-text notes), and link to tickets.

Example sketch of DSL (pseudo-YAML):
  name: cheap-fallback-for-chat
  match: route == \"chat.generate\" and customer_tier != \"enterprise\"
  predicates:
    - token_estimate > 1200
    - latency_window.mean_60s > 150ms
  actions:
    - set_model: mode: \"fallback\" model_hint: \"gptj-6b-q4\"
    - set_max_tokens: 256
  safety:
    - require_response_quality_min: 0.65
  rollout:
    - percent: 20
    - cohorts: [beta_customers, new_signups]

User stories (prioritized):
- As an infra engineer, I can author a policy that forces a cheap model when token_estimate exceeds threshold to control cost.
- As an SRE, I can attach latency-based triggers that route to a regional fallback model when p99 latency exceeds SLO.
- As a product manager, I can A/B a quality gate that runs a small reranker and measure downstream retention impact.
- As compliance, I can add a redact-and-mask action that post-processes outputs for flagged customers.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI: simple editor that validates DSL and previews effective action order.
- Runtime: policy evaluation added to request pipeline with feature-flag gating, p50 overhead < 150us, p99 < 600us for a 3-predicate policy.
- Audit logs created for policy-trigger events (policy_id, version, eval_result, decision).
- Can target policies by route, customer, and tag.
- Rollout controls: percent rollout and kill switch.

Telemetry and metrics to track:
- policy_evals_total, policy_triggers_total, policy_eval_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), cost_delta_estimated_per_hour for affected routes, rollback_rate (auto/manual), downstream_quality_delta (eval harness).

Safety and failure modes (notes):
- Bad predicate might route all traffic to cheap model -> need hard upper/lower bounds or a circuit-breaker that stops policies that increase error rate above threshold.
- Complexity drift: if DSL becomes Turing-complete people will abuse it. Limit to boolean predicates + simple numeric transforms + named actions.
- Cross-policy conflicts: define deterministic priority (explicit weight + creation timestamp fallback). Prefer explicit ordering in UI.

Implementation sketch:
- Authoring UX: editor with live validation + preview on sampled traffic. Save creates versioned artifact stored in config DB (Postgres) and S3 for diffs.
- Runtime: lightweight evaluator in request path written in Go; compile policy to an op-code array for speed. Caching of compiled policies by route+customer_cohort.
- Safety net: automated canary where policy is first run in "observe" mode for N hours, produce telemetry but do not enforce action unless explicitly promoted.
- Integrations: Redwood Console (policy panels), Rollouts (reuse existing rollout infra), Optimize (recommend simple policies based on cost/latency signals).

Experiments to run before MVP:
- Microbenchmark: evaluate overhead of 3 predicate policy running on baseline CPU core (with and without compiled form).
- Simulated traffic: replay production traces and run policy in observe-mode to estimate trigger rates and cost impact.
- UX test: 3 PDs create policies from templates and attempt common tasks (cost cap, latency fallback, redaction). Time-to-complete task + mistakes recorded.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How expressive should predicates be? Allow regex on prompts? Allow embedding similarity predicates? (maybe keep advanced predicates as "pluggable" actions).
- Storage & rollback semantics: soft-rollback vs immutable versions. Need simple promote/rollback flow.
- RBAC: who can author vs who can promote to enforce rollout.
- How to represent stochastic actions (e.g., sample N% of requests for model shadowing)?

Next steps (my immediate checklist):
- Draft initial confluence page with above sketch + UX mockups (Devon to help).
- Run microbenchmark by 2025-11-08 (Ravi volunteering to implement Go evaluator prototype).
- Create GH PR prototype for config artifact schema (RFC PR numbering above).
- Schedule 30-min sync with console team to validate editor constraints.

Notes to self: keep the DSL minimal. Avoid reinventing feature flags. Focus MVP on 3 action types (set_model, set_max_tokens, redact) and 3 predicate types (numeric compare, tag match, windowed metric). Make the observe-first workflow the default so we build trust.

Random brainstormed names: PolicyPad, Composer, Runbook Rules, Hermes (or too mythological?), Heuristix (bad pun). I like "PolicyPad" for the UX and "heuristic-composer" for infra.

End of scratchlog. This is intentionally rough — capture quick ideas and next steps.
